behavior: A population of model agents settles on one shared name without being told to (naming conventions)

sources.citation: Ashery, Aiello and Baronchelli 2025. Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations. Science Advances 11(20), eadu9368.
Saab Jr and Abdallah 2026. Graph Feedback Controls Consensus and Clique Formation in Open-Weight Language-Model Populations.

environment: A simulation trial consists of a population of N interacting agents. At each time-step, two agents are randomly selected for interaction. Each outputs a name from a pool of W names; a match raises both scores and a mismatch lowers both (Ashery et al.).
measure: Success rate, 'the probability of observing a success at a given time' (Ashery et al., Figure 1). Saab Jr and Abdallah report 'Final match', 'the fraction of unordered agent pairs whose final sampled labels agree', and stable consensus over the final 20 rounds.

conditions.name: population size
conditions.value: N=24 (up to 200 in a robustness check)
conditions.passage: we set the name pool size to W=10 and the individual memory length to H=5 for populations of N=24 agents, unless otherwise specified.

conditions.name: name pool
conditions.passage: Agents are asked to select a name from the name pool, which is presented to them as a list of W unique letters sampled from the English alphabet.

conditions.name: payoff
conditions.value: +100 on a match, -50 on a mismatch
conditions.passage: We apply fixed payoffs for successful and failed interactions, set at +100 and -50 points respectively.

conditions.name: pairing
conditions.passage: At each time-step, two agents are randomly selected for interaction.

conditions.name: memory of own interactions
conditions.passage: the prompt provides the LLM agent with a ‘memory’ storing details about the past H interactions they participated in, including their co-player’s convention choice, their own convention choice, whether the interaction was successful or not, and their own accumulated score over these H interactions.

conditions.name: what agents are told about the population
conditions.passage: the prompt does not specify that agents are part of a population or provide any detail on how the interaction partner is selected from a group.

conditions.name: objective
conditions.passage: The objective of each Player is to maximize their own accumulated point tally, conditional on the behavior of the other player.

conditions.name: reasoning instruction
conditions.passage: we prompt the agent to ‘think step by step’ and to explicitly consider the history of play.

conditions.name: order of the names
conditions.passage: Ordering bias is removed by randomizing the list of presented letters for each player at every interaction.

conditions.name: checkpoints
conditions.passage: we simulate these social interactions with four different LLM models: Llama-2-70b-Chat , Llama-3-70B-Instruct , Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct , and Claude-3.5-Sonnet

conditions.name: decoding
conditions.passage: we demand all agents in our experiments to behave non-deterministically by fixing them with a non-zero constant temperature.

reported.statement: Fig. 1 shows that group-wide linguistic conventions spontaneously emerge across all models.
populations as large as N=200 agents reach consensus and that a shared convention emerges for a name pool as large as W=26
The memory is initialized as empty so that, in the first interaction, the output is a random convention chosen from the pool of available names.

mechanism: Ashery et al. base their predictions on 'the naming game model of convention formation, where agents, aiming to coordinate in pairwise interactions, accumulate a memory of past plays, which they then use to “guess” the words their subsequent partners will use'.

retests.statement: random rematching and policies that connect disagreeing groups improve coordination when partner-label history is retained, but not when it is absent.
Homogeneous populations span TinyLlama-1.1B, Yi-1.5-6B, and Qwen2.5 at 7B, 14B, and 32B under the same N=10 , M=10 , T=200 , history, temperature, and state-threshold design.
H=0 replaces the history with an empty-history placeholder, while H=3 and H=10 provide short retained memory.
The implementation and paper-facing reproduction scripts are available at https://github.com/cedar-lau/llm-graph-control .
